# AWS Serverless Metadata Workflow

> An event-driven AWS project that turns Amazon S3 file uploads into normalized DynamoDB metadata records using AWS Lambda.

Canonical site: https://bradleymatera.github.io/Office/
Clean resume link: https://bradleymatera.dev/aws-metadata-workflow/
Repository: https://github.com/BradleyMatera/Office
Portfolio: https://bradleymatera.dev/recruiter/
AWS articles: https://bradleymatera.github.io/Office/writing.html
Project evidence: https://bradleymatera.github.io/Office/proof.html
AWS documentation references: https://bradleymatera.github.io/Office/sources.html

## Core architecture

1. An object is uploaded under a configured Amazon S3 key prefix, defaulting to `incoming/`.
2. S3 sends an object-created notification to AWS Lambda.
3. The Python 3.12 function URL-decodes the key and uses `HeadObject` to read object metadata without downloading the body.
4. It normalizes the metadata into a documented versioned schema.
5. It derives a deterministic SHA-256 `RecordId` from the bucket, decoded key, version ID, and ETag.
6. It writes to DynamoDB with `attribute_not_exists(RecordId)` so repeated event delivery is idempotent.
7. Unexpected failures are raised for Lambda asynchronous retry.
8. Events that still fail are sent to an encrypted SQS failure queue.
9. CloudWatch alarms cover Lambda errors, Lambda throttles, and visible failed events.
10. Optional SNS email alerts require subscription confirmation.

## Verified implementation facts

- Python unit tests: 11 passing in the August 3, 2026 audit.
- Statement and branch coverage: 100% in that audit.
- Infrastructure: AWS SAM and CloudFormation.
- Storage protections: S3 encryption, versioning, ACLs disabled, and Block Public Access enabled.
- Database protections: DynamoDB encryption, on-demand billing, point-in-time recovery, and retained data policy.
- Failure handling: maximum event age, two asynchronous retries, and an encrypted SQS failure destination.
- Site: static GitHub Pages with no runtime AWS credentials and no direct bucket or table access.
- Interface: semantic HTML and CSS following AWS Cloudscape visual foundation and information patterns.

## Internship scope

The original project was completed in isolated AWS internship training and project environments. The public repository does not claim:

- production customer ownership
- live enterprise ticket ownership
- unrestricted Amazon administrative access
- that the public files are exact confidential internship source files
- that a live AWS stack is currently deployed in Bradley Matera's account

## Public description

Bradley Matera built an event-driven AWS metadata workflow during an AWS Support Engineering internship using S3, Lambda, DynamoDB, and a static frontend layer. He created a measurable usage-based cost model and later reconstructed the system publicly with AWS SAM, idempotent writes, retries, a failure queue, monitoring, tests, security controls, diagrams, official AWS references, and technical documentation.
